title.en: The playwright, the setting and the characters

hook.en: Who irons the clothes, cooks the meals and waits up at night in your home, and does anyone say thank you? J.B. Priestley turns this question into a comedy.

objectives.en: Introduce J.B. Priestley and the form of the play
Identify the characters and their traits
State the problem the play sets out to explore

narration.en: Who irons the clothes, cooks the meals and waits up at night in your home, and does anyone say thank you? J.B. Priestley turns this question into a comedy.

body.en: "Mother's Day" is a one-act comedy by J.B. Priestley (1894–1984), an English novelist, playwright and broadcaster known for plays with social themes. It is set in the living room of the Pearson family's suburban house. Beneath the fun, it raises a serious question about how homemakers are treated.

points.en: Form: one-act comedy (with farce and satire)
Serious issue: the unpaid, unrecognised work of mothers

narration.en: "Mother's Day" is a one-act comedy by J.B. Priestley (1894–1984), an English novelist, playwright and broadcaster known for plays with social themes. It is set in the living room of the Pearson family's suburban house. Beneath the fun, it raises a serious question about how homemakers are treated.
Let us map the family around Mrs Pearson.

say.en: At the centre is Mrs Annie Pearson, the meek, overworked mother.
Her neighbour Mrs Fitzgerald is bold and strong, and she tells fortunes.
George, the husband, is self-important and spends his evenings at the club.
Doris, the daughter, expects her mother to serve her.
Cyril, the son, also expects everything to be ready for him.

body.en: Mrs Annie Pearson is a gentle, nervous mother whose husband and grown-up children treat her like a servant. Her neighbour Mrs Fitzgerald is bold, strong-voiced and a fortune-teller. George Pearson is the self-important husband; Doris and Cyril are the selfish grown-up children.

points.en: George: husband, spends evenings at his club
Doris and Cyril: grown-up children who take her for granted

problem.en: What is Mrs Pearson's problem at the beginning of the play?

steps.en: Her husband and grown-up children take her for granted.
She is too gentle to assert herself.

answer.en: Mrs Pearson does all the work at home, but her husband and grown-up children treat her like a servant and never thank her. She is too meek to demand respect, so she asks her neighbour for help.

heading.en: Who is who in the Pearson house

body.en: Link each Pearson to what they want from Annie: George wants his tea before the club, Doris wants her dress ironed, Cyril wants his things ready. Mrs Fitzgerald is the one who wants something FOR Annie.
